findings.finding: The second Fenja tranche that the 'runway into Q3 2027' guide rests on is capped at 10% of market cap at drawdown. At ~SEK 16 x 56.2m shares (~SEK 900m) the total cap is ~SEK 90m, so at most ~SEK 40m of the second SEK 50m is available. In July, at ~SEK 20, the full SEK 100m fit. The Q3 report has to restate the runway or the funding plan against a smaller tranche.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Report days that carried financing news moved hard. Q2 2026 (20 Aug, the report after the Fenja facility) fell 9.93%. Q1 2025 fell 18.65%. Both are MFN day stats; the causes were not isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: No analyst publishes the cap arithmetic. Edison writes only 'subject to a market-cap cap'. If it were priced, the 10% slide since 27 Oct would already be read as a funding problem and the short register would be building. It reads 1.33%, unchanged since 7 Sep. The effect is small, about a third of one quarter's burn, and is partly offset by the SEK 8m tax credit due in November. Financing question asked: the money buys Phase 3 readiness ahead of partnering, so this is runway, not distress, and it is sized small.
findings.independence: Edison BM-3854 confirms the remaining tranche is 'available for drawdown in Q426 at the company's discretion and subject to a market-cap cap' (https://www.edisongroup.com/research/broader-resomelagon-opportunity-taking-shape/BM-3854/). Same underlying terms, so this is not independent evidence for the sign.
